testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Transporting hanging meat in a refrigerated truck requires special care because:

options.text: It is a good way for new drivers to gain experience.
It is illegal in most states.

questions.explanation: Hanging meat is an unstable load. It has a high center of gravity, and the meat can swing around. This makes the vehicle harder to control.

questions.question: Before driving down a hill, you should shift into a ____ gear.
questions.explanation: Shift into a low gear before going downhill. Gravity will make your vehicle go faster on the hill, so a low gear helps you stay in control.

questions.question: Backing up with a trailer is dangerous because:

options.text: It is hard to see behind the vehicle.
Most trucks cannot move in reverse.
Cargo may fall out of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to see behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Backing up is dangerous because the driver cannot see everything behind the truck. Avoid backing up whenever possible.

questions.question: When transporting cargo, you must check that it is secure every:
questions.explanation: Check cargo security within the first 50 miles of a trip. Then check it again every three hours or 150 miles, whichever comes first.

questions.question: While driving, ____ keeps spring brakes from activating.
questions.explanation: Air pressure holds spring brakes in place while you drive. If air pressure drops too low, the springs will activate the brakes.

questions.question: Braking mechanisms are located inside:
questions.explanation: Brake drums are attached to the wheels on the axles. The parts that make the vehicle stop are inside the brake drum.

questions.question: To prevent hydroplaning on wet roads, you should:

options.text: Keep your tires with good tread depth.
Let air out of your tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your tires with good tread depth.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning risk increases with low tire pressure and worn tire tread. Good tread depth helps your tires grip wet roads better.

questions.question: During the driving test, the examiner scores you on:

options.text: How fast you reach your destination

questions.explanation: The examiner scores your driving maneuvers and your general driving behavior during the on-road test.

questions.question: To change lanes safely, you should:
questions.explanation: Change lanes slowly and smoothly. This gives other drivers time to see you and move if needed. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: While driving a CMV, you:

options.text: May hold a cell phone to receive a call
Cannot hold a cell phone to make a call

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot hold a cell phone to make a call
questions.explanation: Do not hold a cell phone to make calls while driving a CMV. Do not send or read text messages while driving.

questions.question: When driving on packed snow, how much should you reduce your speed?
questions.explanation: Packed snow reduces grip on the road. Reduce your speed by one-half or more when driving on packed snow.

questions.question: What should you know about trains near a railroad crossing?

options.text: You will hear every approaching train.
You may not hear a train, even if one is approaching.
You will hear two short horn blasts if a train is approaching.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not hear a train, even if one is approaching.
questions.explanation: Do not assume you will hear a train. The operator may not sound the horn, or the horn may be prohibited in that area. Noise inside your vehicle may prevent you from hearing a train until it is too close.

questions.question: If a police officer asks you to take a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) test:

options.text: You can refuse without any penalty.
You can refuse but must pay a $50 fine.
You will lose your CDL if you refuse.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will lose your CDL if you refuse.
questions.explanation: Most states have an Implied Consent Law. By driving on state roads, you agree to take a drug or alcohol test if asked. If you refuse, you will lose your driving privileges. Know the laws for every state where you drive.

questions.question: In hot weather, where tar is bleeding through the pavement:

options.text: The grip is the same as the rest of the road.
The grip is better than the rest of the road.

questions.explanation: In very hot weather, tar rises to the road surface. These spots are very slippery. Watch for them and be careful.

questions.question: Where should regrooved tires NOT be used?

options.text: On the front wheels of a bus

questions.correctAnswerText: On the front wheels of a bus
questions.explanation: Regrooved, recapped, or retreaded tires cannot be used on the front wheels of a bus.

questions.question: In heavy traffic, what is the safest speed to drive?

options.text: The speed of the traffic around you
Much slower than the surrounding traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: The speed of the traffic around you
questions.explanation: In heavy traffic, match the speed of surrounding vehicles. Cars moving at the same speed in the same direction are less likely to crash. Never exceed the speed limit, though.

questions.question: In cold weather, how often should you check your vehicle's alcohol evaporator?
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator prevents ice from building up in the air brake system. In cold weather, check and refill it every day.

questions.question: When should the low air pressure warning signal turn on?
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, the low air pressure warning signal must activate when tank pressure falls below 60 psi. The warning may be a light, buzzer, or wig wag.

questions.question: When should you adjust your mirrors?

options.text: When stopped at a traffic signal

questions.explanation: Adjust and check your mirrors before each trip. Any attached trailer should be straight when you adjust your mirrors.

questions.question: Which behavior shows aggressive driving?

options.text: Slowing down and keeping a safe distance from other vehicles
Making hand gestures that could anger other drivers

questions.correctAnswerText: Making hand gestures that could anger other drivers
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, plan extra time for delays, keep a safe distance from other vehicles, and do not make hand gestures that could anger other drivers.

questions.question: What type of force do emergency brakes use?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three parts: service brake, parking brake, and emergency brake. Emergency and parking brakes use mechanical force.

questions.question: When should you check your mirrors?

options.text: When changing lanes, but only when other vehicles are nearby.
When changing lanes, but only if it is dark outside.

questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors before changing lanes. Mirror checks should be part of your regular driving routine.

questions.question: To avoid a hazard, you:

options.text: Should always come to a complete stop.
May need to steer around it.

questions.correctAnswerText: May need to steer around it.
questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the best way to avoid a hazard. If you don't have enough space to stop, steering around it may be your safest option.

questions.question: Which is an example of required emergency equipment?
questions.explanation: All commercial vehicles must have proper emergency equipment. This includes spare electrical fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one fire extinguisher.

questions.question: If you are not sure how to put out a vehicle fire, you should:
questions.explanation: If you are unsure which type of fire extinguisher to use, especially for hazardous materials fires, wait for firefighters to arrive and handle it.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a sign of fatigue?
questions.explanation: Signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, frequent blinking, yawning, rubbing your eyes, daydreaming, trouble remembering the last few miles, missing exits, drifting from your lane, and following too closely. Staying in your lane is safe driving behavior, not a sign of fatigue.

questions.question: What is the maximum safe air loss rate for a single vehicle with air brakes during a leakage test?
questions.explanation: A single vehicle with air brakes should not lose more than 3 psi in one minute during a leakage test.

questions.question: Brake linings should be:
questions.explanation: Brake linings should not be loose or soaked with oil or grease. They should not be too thin.

questions.question: Why is it important to watch the road ahead?

options.text: It gives you time to plan how to avoid hazards.
It is not encouraged because it distracts you.
It is only important in heavy traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to plan how to avoid hazards.
questions.explanation: Always watch for hazards ahead. This gives you time to react before you reach the hazard.

questions.question: Which vehicle requires a driver to have a CDL?
questions.explanation: A CDL is not required for military vehicles, emergency vehicles, farm equipment, or recreational vehicles. School buses require a CDL.

questions.question: While driving, which statement about texting is true?

options.text: You cannot send a text, but you can read one.
You can send a text, but you cannot read one.
You cannot send or read a text.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot send or read a text.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is not allowed. Texting includes typing on an electronic device or reading messages from one.

questions.question: When you start an engine, how long should it take for oil pressure to reach normal?
questions.explanation: When you start the engine, check the gauges. Oil pressure should reach normal within seconds of starting.

questions.question: A five-foot cargo item on a flatbed trailer must be secured by at least how many tie-downs?
questions.explanation: Cargo needs one tie-down for every 10 feet of length. However, always use at least two tie-downs, even for small cargo.

questions.question: When driving, what is most important to do?

options.text: Plan how to handle dangerous situations before they happen.
Turn your head around instead of using mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan how to handle dangerous situations before they happen.
questions.explanation: Always watch the road for hazards. Think ahead about what you will do if a hazard becomes an emergency.

questions.question: What happens when a vehicle hydroplanes?

options.text: The tires lose contact with the road.
The trailer disconnects from the tractor.
The vehicle becomes easier to control.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tires lose contact with the road.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, tires can lose grip and slide on water. This is hydroplaning. It can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph.

questions.question: When driving at night, which of these should you NOT do?

options.text: Make sure your glasses are clean.

questions.explanation: Do not wear sunglasses at night. Clean your eyeglasses if you wear them. Make sure you are well-rested before driving at night.

questions.question: A cardboard box on the roadway:

options.text: Is something you should expect to see.
Could hold a heavy object that damages vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Could hold a heavy object that damages vehicles.
questions.explanation: Any object on the road is a danger. Even a cardboard box might contain something hard or heavy that could damage your vehicle.

questions.question: When getting out of a vehicle, a driver should:

options.text: Jump directly from the seat to the ground.
Keep at least one hand on the vehicle.

questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle, you must face it and keep three points of contact at all times. On a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may cause you to fail the vehicle control skills test.

questions.question: When checking your windshield before a trip, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Remove and sharpen the wiper blades.
Check the wiper arms for proper tension.
Check the wiper blades for damage.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove and sharpen the wiper blades.
questions.explanation: Check your windshield for cracks or damage that blocks your view. Check wiper arms for proper tension and wiper blades for damage or cracks.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver has a crash ahead of you, what should you do?

options.text: Stop safely away from the crash, wait for police, and tell them about the aggressive driving.
Block the driver in with your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely away from the crash, wait for police, and tell them about the aggressive driving.
questions.explanation: If you see an aggressive driver in a crash, stop a safe distance away. Wait for police to arrive and tell them what aggressive behavior you saw.

questions.question: When you start a vehicle, warning lights and buzzers should:

options.text: Not turn on or make any sound.
Turn on, then turn off quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on, then turn off quickly.
questions.explanation: When you start your engine, warning lights and buzzers should turn on briefly, then shut off right away.

questions.question: When entering a curve, you should:
questions.explanation: Before entering a curve, slow down to a safe speed and shift into a lower gear.

questions.question: Transporting hanging meat in a trailer is challenging because:

options.text: It is not recommended during summer months.
The load has a high center of gravity.

questions.correctAnswerText: The load has a high center of gravity.
questions.explanation: Hanging meat is unstable because it has a high center of gravity. The meat can also swing, which makes it harder to control the vehicle.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing during a driving test, you should:

options.text: Pass another slow-moving vehicle on the tracks.
Change lanes while on the tracks.
Not change gears while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not change gears while on the tracks.
questions.explanation: During a driving test, do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on railroad tracks.

questions.question: When visibility is poor and you are driving near other vehicles, you should:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when visibility is poor and other drivers are near you, such as at dawn, dusk, or in bad weather. High beams can make it hard for other drivers to see.

questions.question: During winter, what should you check extra carefully in a pre-trip inspection?
questions.explanation: In winter, check coolant and antifreeze levels, defrosting and heating equipment, wiper blades, windshield washer fluid, tires, tire chains, lights, mirrors, windows, and the exhaust system.

questions.question: For a triple combination vehicle, the maximum air leakage rate during a test is ____ per minute.
questions.explanation: A triple combination vehicle should have an air leakage rate of no more than 6 psi per minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: The more alcohol in your body:

options.text: The faster your liver will process it.
The less effect it will have on you.
The longer it will take to leave your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer it will take to leave your body.
questions.explanation: Your body removes alcohol at a fixed rate. The more alcohol you drink, the longer it takes your body to remove it.

questions.question: Bracing is used to:

options.text: Make cargo stand taller in a trailer.
Stop cargo from moving in a trailer.
Make it easier to unload cargo from a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop cargo from moving in a trailer.
questions.explanation: Blocking and bracing prevent cargo from shifting during transport. Blocking is placed in front, behind, and to the sides of cargo. Bracing runs from the top of cargo down to the trailer floor and sides.

questions.question: If brakes get too hot:

options.text: They may squeak more than usual.

questions.explanation: Too much heat can cause brakes to fade and lose their stopping power. Do not rely only on brakes to slow your vehicle. Use engine braking to help cool the brakes.
